title: Ex 3.5 #12 · Splitting 21 people into teams of 10 and 11
prompt: Twenty-one people are split into a Red Team of 10 people and a Blue Team of 11 people. In how many ways can this be done?
answer_format: A whole number, or an expression for it like 26^4 or binom(10, 3).

mistakes.hint: Choosing the Red Team already decides the Blue Team (it's everyone else), so there is nothing extra to count.
The order in which the Red Team members are picked doesn't matter.
The teams have different names and different sizes, so no split is counted twice. There is nothing to divide out.

hints: Once you know who is on the Red Team, is there any further choice to make?
Count the ways to choose the 10 Red Team members from the 21 people.
solution: A split is determined by the Red Team: choose its 10 members, and the other 11 people form the Blue Team.
So there are $\binom{21}{10} = 352{,}716$ splits. (Choosing the Blue Team first gives $\binom{21}{11}$, the same number.)

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses combinations (Section 3.5).
